newsitem.title: FRANCE: French farmers dump imported fruit and vegetables.
newsitem.headline: French farmers dump imported fruit and vegetables.

text.p: French farmers dumped tonnes of imported fruit and vegetables in the streets of several cities and trashed markets in Nantes and Marseille on Thursday in protest at a flood of low-price foreign produce.
In Nantes, western France, some 100 to 150 farmers stopped lorries loaded with Spanish melons and potatoes and dumped their cargoes on the ground.

Others burned crates of fruit in front of the town hall and went on a rampage through the local wholesale market, tipping over stacks of produce crates and breaking up some market stands, police and witnesses said.
The farmers left after talks with the director of the market.
About 200-300 farmers in Marseille went on a similar rampage in the wholesale market in the Mediterranean port, police said.
"This is a protest to show the exasperation of producers over imports, especially from Spain and Morocco ... at real discount prices," one farmer said.
In Avignon in southern France, farmers set fire to stacks of crates containing fruit.

The dumping of imported fruit and vegetables has become a common form of protest in France. French workers want measures to counteract factors such as lower foreign labour costs that they say undercut their prices.
